lessons.title: Language Practice: Revision of Future Tense
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

English has several ways to talk about the future. Will/shall + base verb is used for future facts, promises and decisions: They will come here again next year; I shall complain to the principal sometime next week. Future Continuous (will/shall be + verb-ing) shows an action in progress at a future time: They will be watching the cricket match tonight. Future Perfect (will/shall have + past participle) shows an action completed by a future time, usually with 'by': We shall have climbed the mountain by tomorrow afternoon. Be going to is used for plans and for predictions from present signs: Tariq is going to deliver the speech; Look at that car! It is going to crash. The Present Continuous is used for fixed arrangements: We are taking a trip to Tharparkar next Sunday. The Present Simple is used for timetables: The train leaves in half an hour. In time clauses after when, until, by the time and if, use the Present Simple for the future, not will: He will visit us when he comes to Karachi; It will cost a lot more if we buy it next year.

Examples

SentenceFuture form
They will come here again next year.will + base verb
We shall be in trouble for being late.shall + base verb
I shall be appearing for my board exams this year.Future Continuous
He will be staying home the whole evening.Future Continuous
He will have had his tooth pulled out by the time we reach.Future Perfect
By the time we finish they will have left.Future Perfect
We are going to cut this tree as it is about to fall.be going to
The tree is going to shed its leaves soon as it is autumn time.be going to
They are buying a new house soon.Present Continuous (arrangement)
The ship sails for South Africa next week.Present Simple (timetable)
We will wait for you at the gate until you arrive.will + present simple in time clause
Dad will be waiting for you at the station when you arrive next week.Future Continuous + time clause
By the end of this year, I will have visited Brazil.Future Perfect
Sara and Meena will have finished their IT project by tomorrow afternoon.Future Perfect

Remember

Choose the form by meaning: plan or sign → going to; fixed arrangement → present continuous; timetable → present simple; in progress then → future continuous; completed by then → future perfect. In Exercise 4, groups discuss 'As I see Pakistan in fifteen years' time': a developed and peaceful country, better schools and hospitals, jobs for all, clean green cities, solar energy and saved water.

options: An action in progress at a future time
An action completed by a future time
mcqs.q: Will/shall + base verb is used for:
mcqs.why: The rules say will/shall + base verb is used for future facts, promises and decisions: 'They will come here again next year.' Other future forms handle progress, completion, plans and timetables.

mcqs.q: 'They will be watching the cricket match tonight' uses:
mcqs.why: This is Future Continuous: will/shall be + verb-ing, showing an action in progress at a future time. Tonight the watching will be in progress, not simply beginning or completed.

mcqs.q: 'We shall have climbed the mountain by tomorrow afternoon' uses:
mcqs.why: This is Future Perfect: will/shall have + past participle, showing an action completed by a future time, usually with 'by'. By tomorrow afternoon the climbing will already be finished.

options: Plans, and predictions from present signs
mcqs.q: 'Be going to' is used for:
mcqs.why: The rules say 'be going to' is used for plans and for predictions from present signs: 'Tariq is going to deliver the speech' (plan) and 'Look at that car! It is going to crash' (prediction from a sign).

options: Present Continuous, for a fixed arrangement
will + base verb, for a promise
mcqs.q: 'We are taking a trip to Tharparkar next Sunday' uses:
mcqs.why: The Present Continuous is used for fixed arrangements, as the matching example 'They are buying a new house soon' also shows. The trip is already arranged, so present continuous is chosen.

mcqs.q: 'The train ___ in half an hour' — which form fits the timetable rule?
mcqs.why: The example is 'The train leaves in half an hour': the Present Simple is used for timetables. The same rule gives 'The ship sails for South Africa next week' in the examples table.

mcqs.q: In 'He will visit us when he ___ to Karachi', the time clause takes:
mcqs.why: In time clauses after when, until, by the time and if, we use the Present Simple for the future, not will: 'He will visit us when he comes to Karachi.' The main clause keeps 'will visit'.

options: be going to for a plan
Future Perfect: 'By the time we finish they will have left'
mcqs.q: Which sentence is Future Perfect?
mcqs.why: 'By the time we finish they will have left' is listed as Future Perfect: will have + left, completed by that future moment. 'By the end of this year, I will have visited Brazil' follows the same pattern.

mcqs.q: 'I shall be appearing for my board exams this year' is:
mcqs.why: The examples table marks this Future Continuous: shall be + appearing, an action that will be in progress over a future period. Compare 'He will be staying home the whole evening.'

options: in progress at a future time → future continuous
plan or sign → present continuous only
mcqs.q: Choose the correct meaning-to-form matching from the Remember section:
mcqs.why: The Remember section says: plan or sign → going to; fixed arrangement → present continuous; timetable → present simple; in progress then → future continuous; completed by then → future perfect.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Active and Passive Voice
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

In the active voice, the subject does the action: The officer has sent the official documents. In the passive voice, the subject receives the action: The official documents have been sent by the officer. To change active into passive: make the object the subject, use the correct form of 'be' + past participle, and add 'by + doer' if needed. The tense stays the same. To change passive into active: make the doer the subject and use the matching active verb form. When the doer is unknown in a passive sentence, a sensible doer is supplied: 'The thieves were caught' becomes 'The police caught the thieves.'

Passive into Active

PassiveActive
The walls are being painted by them.They are painting the walls.
The latest book of the writer is liked by the readers.The readers like the latest book of the writer.
We had been given the wrong tickets.They had given us the wrong tickets.
These three books had been written by him in 1873.He had written these three books in 1873.
Why is time wasted by everyone?Why does everyone waste time?
The new houses will be built by the new construction company.The new construction company will build the new houses.
They can be given some information about the job by Ramiz.Ramiz can give them some information about the job.
A new road was being planned near my house by the government.The government was planning a new road near my house.

Active into Passive

ActivePassive
Students should study environmental problems at school.Environmental problems should be studied by students at school.
Teachers could include this topic in their classes.This topic could be included in their classes by teachers.
Governments have constantly ignored important issues for economic reasons.Important issues have been constantly ignored by governments for economic reasons.
At school, teachers often tell students about pollution and its prevention.At school, students are often told about pollution and its prevention by teachers.
Everyone should throw their bottles in the bottle recycling bins.Their bottles should be thrown in the bottle recycling bins by everyone.
Parents must teach their children how to dispose the rubbish.Children must be taught how to dispose the rubbish by parents.
Last year several nations held a meeting to discuss environmental problems.Last year a meeting was held by several nations to discuss environmental problems.
Organizations like Greenpeace are giving people leaflets about what to do.People are being given leaflets about what to do by organizations like Greenpeace.

Remember

Keep the tense unchanged when you change the voice, and keep both objects where a verb has two: 'Ramiz can give them some information' — them → they can be given…; some information can also become the subject. Exercise 7 changes the voice of whole passages: the jewellery shop robbery (passive to active) and the school contest (active to passive).

options: The verb is always in the past
mcqs.q: In the active voice:
mcqs.why: In the active voice, the subject does the action: 'The officer has sent the official documents.' In the passive voice, the subject receives the action: 'The official documents have been sent by the officer.'

options: Change the tense to the past
Make the object the subject, use the correct form of 'be' + past participle, and add 'by + doer' if needed
mcqs.q: To change an active sentence into the passive voice, you:
mcqs.why: The rule is: make the object the subject, use the correct form of 'be' + past participle, and add 'by + doer' if needed. The tense stays the same during the change.

mcqs.q: What happens to the tense when the voice is changed?
mcqs.why: The rules and the Remember section both stress: the tense stays the same when you change the voice. 'He had written these three books in 1873' becomes 'had been written', keeping the past perfect.

options: 'They are painting the walls' is the passive form of the sentence
'They are painting the walls' is the active form of 'The walls are being painted by them'
mcqs.q: Which statement is correct?
mcqs.why: The table pairs the passive 'The walls are being painted by them' with the active 'They are painting the walls.' The doer becomes the subject and the verb takes its matching active form, present continuous in both.

options: Someone gave us the wrong tickets (any doer)
'They had given us the wrong tickets' — a sensible doer is supplied
mcqs.q: 'We had been given the wrong tickets' becomes, in active voice:
mcqs.why: When the doer is unknown in a passive sentence, a sensible doer is supplied, and the table gives 'They had given us the wrong tickets.' The same method turns 'The thieves were caught' into 'The police caught the thieves.'

options: Environmental problems should be studied by students at school
Students should be studied by environmental problems at school
Environmental problems should study by students at school
Environmental problems are should studied by students at school
mcqs.q: 'Students should study environmental problems at school' in passive voice is:
mcqs.why: The object 'environmental problems' becomes the subject, and 'should study' becomes 'should be studied': 'Environmental problems should be studied by students at school.' This is exactly the form given in the lesson's table.

options: A meeting was held by several nations to discuss environmental problems
Several nations were held a meeting
A meeting is hold by nations
mcqs.q: 'Last year several nations held a meeting' in passive voice is:
mcqs.why: The table gives: 'Last year a meeting was held by several nations to discuss environmental problems.' The past tense 'held' becomes 'was held', keeping the same tense in passive form.

options: 'People are being given leaflets about what to do by organizations like Greenpeace'
mcqs.q: 'Organizations like Greenpeace are giving people leaflets' in passive voice is:
mcqs.why: With two objects, either can become the subject; the table chooses 'people': 'People are being given leaflets about what to do by organizations like Greenpeace.' The present continuous passive keeps 'are being given'.

mcqs.q: 'Why is time wasted by everyone?' in active voice is:
mcqs.why: The table converts the question to 'Why does everyone waste time?' The doer 'everyone' becomes the subject, and the question form 'does… waste' matches the present simple tense.

options: Only the first object can ever be used
'Them' becomes 'they can be given…', and 'some information' can also become the subject
Questions cannot be changed into passive
mcqs.q: What does the Remember section say about verbs with two objects, like 'Ramiz can give them some information'?
mcqs.why: The Remember section says to keep both objects where a verb has two: 'them' becomes 'they can be given some information', and 'some information' can also become the subject of the passive sentence.

lessons.title: Writing: Cause and Effect Essay
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 4.4 Writing teaches the cause and effect essay. First, sentences are built from a cause, a connector and an effect, and split back into cause and effect. Useful connectors: so, therefore, hence, consequently, due to that, because, as. Then a cause-effect diagram is drawn for a topic — causes, effects and suggestions — and finally a four-to-five paragraph essay is written from the diagram.

Cause and Effect in Sentences

CauseEffect
I never brush my teethI have five cavities (so)
The streets were snow-packed and icyCars needed more time to stop (due to that)
His arm was brokenThe doctor put it in a cast (hence)
A football player violated the rules of the gameThe referee called a penalty (consequently)
Your dog bit a childHe got a deep wound (therefore)
I skipped lunch todayI am extremely hungry (so)
My best friend lied to meI have difficulty trusting people (because)
She forgot to water her plantsThey all died (hence)
He won the raceThe player has received a gold medal (as)
He did not study for the testHe failed it (consequently)

Cause-Effect Diagrams

TopicCausesEffectsSuggestions
Lavish spendings on weddingsShowing off wealth; social pressure and competitionHeavy debts; wastage of money and foodKeep weddings simple; spend on the couple's future
High cost of medical servicesExpensive medicines and equipment; shortage of public hospitalsPoor cannot afford treatment; people avoid going to doctorsMore government hospitals; control prices of medicines
Migration from rural to urban areasLack of jobs and facilities in villages; better education and health care in citiesOvercrowding in cities; villages lose workersDevelop villages; provide jobs and facilities in rural areas

Model Essay: Lavish Spendings on Weddings

In our society, weddings have become a show of wealth. Families spend huge amounts of money on decorations, food, clothes and halls. This lavish spending has many causes and effects. The main causes are showing off wealth and social pressure. Families want to impress their relatives and neighbours, and they compete with one another. As a result, they spend far more than they can afford. The effects are harmful. Many families take loans and fall into debt. A lot of food is wasted, and the money spent could have been used for the couple's future. To solve this problem, weddings should be kept simple. Families should spend only what they can afford and use the saved money for the new couple's home and education. In conclusion, a simple wedding brings more happiness than a lavish one.

Model Essay: High Cost of Medical Services

Medical treatment has become very expensive in our country. Poor people often cannot afford to see a doctor or buy medicines. The high cost of medical services has many causes. First, medicines and medical equipment are expensive. Secondly, there are too few public hospitals, so people must go to costly private hospitals. Thirdly, some doctors charge high fees. The effects are serious. Poor patients delay treatment, and their illnesses become worse. Some families borrow money or sell their belongings to pay hospital bills. To solve this problem, the government should build more hospitals and provide free or cheap treatment. The prices of medicines should be controlled. In conclusion, cheap and good medical care is the right of every citizen.

Model Essay: Migration of People from Rural to Urban Areas

Every year, many people leave their villages and move to cities. This migration from rural to urban areas is increasing. The causes are clear. Villages lack jobs, good schools, hospitals and other facilities. In cities, people hope to find work, better education and better health care. As a result, cities are becoming overcrowded. Houses, transport, water and electricity fall short, and pollution increases. At the same time, villages lose their young and able workers, and farming suffers. To solve this problem, villages must be developed. The government should provide jobs, schools, hospitals, clean water and electricity in rural areas. If village life becomes comfortable, fewer people will migrate. In conclusion, balanced development of villages and cities will make migration a choice, not a need.

Remember

Essay structure: introduction of the issue, a paragraph of causes, a paragraph of effects, suggestions, and a conclusion — the diagram becomes the essay, paragraph by paragraph.

options: A cause, a connector and an effect
mcqs.q: In this lesson, sentences are first built from:
mcqs.why: Unit 4.4 first builds sentences from a cause, a connector and an effect, and then splits them back into cause and effect. Useful connectors are so, therefore, hence, consequently, due to that, because and as.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a cause-effect connector used in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The connectors listed are so, therefore, hence, consequently, due to that, because and as. For example, 'I never brush my teeth (so) I have five cavities' joins a cause to its effect with 'so'.

mcqs.q: 'Your dog bit a child' — what is the effect in the lesson's table?
mcqs.why: The table pairs the cause 'Your dog bit a child' with the effect 'He got a deep wound', joined by 'therefore'. Each row of the table matches one cause with its own effect.

options: She forgot to water her plants
The weather was too hot only
mcqs.q: What caused the plants to die in one example?
mcqs.why: The cause given is 'She forgot to water her plants', and the effect is 'They all died', joined by 'hence'. Forgetting the water, not the weather, is the stated cause.

options: Showing off wealth and social pressure and competition
mcqs.q: What are the causes of lavish spending on weddings in the diagram?
mcqs.why: The diagram lists the causes as showing off wealth, and social pressure and competition. The effects are heavy debts and wastage of money and food, and the suggestion is to keep weddings simple.

options: More government hospitals and controlling the prices of medicines
mcqs.q: What suggestions does the diagram give for the high cost of medical services?
mcqs.why: The suggestions are: more government hospitals and control prices of medicines. The causes are expensive medicines and equipment and a shortage of public hospitals, which the suggestions directly answer.

options: Overcrowding in cities, and villages lose workers
mcqs.q: What are the effects of migration from rural to urban areas?
mcqs.why: The diagram lists the effects as overcrowding in cities and villages losing workers. People migrate because villages lack jobs and facilities while cities offer better education and health care.

options: Families want to impress their relatives and neighbours and compete with one another
mcqs.q: In the model essay, why do families spend so much on weddings?
mcqs.why: The essay says the main causes are showing off wealth and social pressure: families want to impress their relatives and neighbours and compete with one another, so they spend far more than they can afford.

options: Poor patients delay treatment and their illnesses become worse; some families borrow money or sell belongings
Doctors lower their fees at once
mcqs.q: What effects of costly medical care does the model essay describe?
mcqs.why: The essay says poor patients delay treatment and their illnesses become worse, and some families borrow money or sell their belongings to pay hospital bills. Cheap and good medical care is called the right of every citizen.

options: only causes, then a list of words
introduction of the issue, causes, effects, suggestions, and a conclusion
mcqs.q: What is the structure of a cause and effect essay?
mcqs.why: The Remember section gives the structure: introduction of the issue, a paragraph of causes, a paragraph of effects, suggestions, and a conclusion — the diagram becomes the essay, paragraph by paragraph.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 4.5 Study Skills teaches critical thinking and problem solving: for each problem, ask why it exists, then suggest possible solutions. The same steps are then applied to major problems of Pakistan, with a cluster developed for each problem.

School Problems and Solutions

ProblemWhy it existsPossible solution
Bullying in schoolsSome students want power or have problems at home; rules are not strictStrict school rules against bullying; teachers watch and counsel bullies and victims; students report bullying to teachers
Incomplete homeworkStudents do not understand the work, waste time, or have too much workTeachers explain clearly and give reasonable homework; students make a timetable; parents check homework
Talkativeness in classStudents are bored or want attention; lessons are not interestingMake lessons interesting and interactive; give talkative students class duties; set class rules
Littering in schoolNo dustbins nearby; students do not carePlace dustbins everywhere; run a clean-school campaign; make students responsible for their classrooms
Late coming to schoolStudents sleep late; no transportGo to bed early; parents ensure timely transport; the school keeps a record of latecomers

Major Problems of Pakistan

ProblemWhy it existsSolutions
Load-sheddingShortage of power plants, line losses, and wastage of electricityBuild solar and wind power plants; save electricity; stop electricity theft
IlliteracyPoverty, too few schools, and children working instead of studyingFree primary education for all; more schools and trained teachers; awareness among parents
PollutionVehicles, factories, and plastic bagsPlant more trees; improve public transport; ban plastic bags and control factory smoke

Remember

Critical thinking means: name the problem, find why it exists, and only then suggest solutions that match the causes.

options: Ask why it exists, then suggest possible solutions
mcqs.q: In critical thinking and problem solving, what do you do for each problem first?
mcqs.why: The lesson teaches: for each problem, ask why it exists, then suggest possible solutions. The Remember section repeats the order — name the problem, find why it exists, and only then suggest solutions that match the causes.

options: Some students want power or have problems at home; rules are not strict
mcqs.q: Why does bullying exist in schools, according to the table?
mcqs.why: The table says bullying exists because some students want power or have problems at home, and rules are not strict. The solutions match these causes: strict rules, teacher watching and counselling, and reporting.

options: Teachers explain clearly and give reasonable homework; students make a timetable; parents check homework
mcqs.q: What is the solution for incomplete homework?
mcqs.why: The table's solutions are: teachers explain clearly and give reasonable homework; students make a timetable; parents check homework. The causes are not understanding the work, wasting time, or having too much work.

options: Students should sit silently all day
Make lessons interesting and interactive, give talkative students class duties, and set class rules
mcqs.q: How can talkativeness in class be handled?
mcqs.why: Talkativeness comes from boredom or wanting attention, so the solutions are: make lessons interesting and interactive, give talkative students class duties, and set class rules. The energy is used, not just punished.

options: No dustbins nearby, and students do not care
mcqs.q: Why does littering happen in school?
mcqs.why: The table gives the causes of littering in school as: no dustbins nearby, and students do not care. Solutions follow from these causes — place dustbins everywhere and run a clean-school campaign.

options: Students sleep late, and there is no transport
mcqs.q: Why do students come late to school?
mcqs.why: The causes listed are that students sleep late and there is no transport. The matched solutions are: go to bed early, parents ensure timely transport, and the school keeps a record of latecomers.

options: Shortage of power plants, line losses, and wastage of electricity
mcqs.q: Why does load-shedding exist in Pakistan?
mcqs.why: The major-problems table lists the causes of load-shedding as shortage of power plants, line losses, and wastage of electricity. The solutions are to build solar and wind power plants, save electricity, and stop electricity theft.

options: Poverty, too few schools, and children working instead of studying
mcqs.q: What causes illiteracy, according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: Illiteracy exists because of poverty, too few schools, and children working instead of studying. The solutions match: free primary education for all, more schools and trained teachers, and awareness among parents.

mcqs.q: What causes pollution in the major-problems table?
mcqs.why: The table lists vehicles, factories, and plastic bags as the causes of pollution. Solutions include planting more trees, improving public transport, banning plastic bags and controlling factory smoke.

options: Name the problem, find why it exists, and only then suggest solutions that match the causes
mcqs.q: What does critical thinking mean in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The Remember section defines it exactly: name the problem, find why it exists, and only then suggest solutions that match the causes. Solutions that ignore causes do not solve the problem.

lessons.title: Fun: Me After 10 Years
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 4.6 Fun asks you to complete the sentence 'In ten years' time, I see myself becoming an/a …' using one of the given careers, and to present it to the class: choose an uncommon profession, state what you will become, what you will have to do to become that, why you want to become that, and how it will help you in your future life.

Careers to Choose From

An astronaut, a ship captain, an anthropologist, a marine biologist, a linguist, a chef, a judge, a nutritionist, a veterinarian, a physiotherapist, an agronomist, a web developer, a submarine captain, a journalist, a wildlife photographer, a mountain climber, a tourist guide, a museum caretaker, a herbalist.

Model Presentations

A journalist: In ten years' time, I see myself becoming a journalist. I will study hard, complete my education, and work for a newspaper. I will write true stories and share useful information with people.

A marine biologist: In ten years' time, I see myself becoming a marine biologist. A marine biologist is a person who studies living things in seas and oceans. To become one, I will have to study biology, learn swimming and diving, and complete a degree in marine science. I want to become a marine biologist because I love the sea and its creatures. It will help me in my future life because I will have a good job, and I will help protect sea life and keep our oceans clean.

Remember

Use the correct article with the career: 'a journalist', 'a chef', but 'an astronaut', 'an anthropologist', 'an agronomist'.

mcqs.why: The lesson instructs: choose an uncommon profession, state what you will become, what you will have to do to become that, why you want to become that, and how it will help you in your future life.

mcqs.q: Which sentence must you complete in this activity?
mcqs.why: The Fun lesson asks you to complete the sentence 'In ten years' time, I see myself becoming an/a …' using one of the given careers, and then present it to the class.

mcqs.q: Which phrase uses the correct article?
mcqs.why: The Remember section warns: use 'a journalist', 'a chef', but 'an astronaut', 'an anthropologist', 'an agronomist'. Astronaut begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'.

options: A person who studies living things in seas and oceans
A person who treats sick animals
mcqs.q: What is a marine biologist?
mcqs.why: The model presentation defines it: a marine biologist is a person who studies living things in seas and oceans. To become one, the student will study biology, learn swimming and diving, and complete a degree in marine science.

options: Study biology, learn swimming and diving, and complete a degree in marine science
mcqs.q: What will the student have to do to become a marine biologist?
mcqs.why: The model says: 'I will have to study biology, learn swimming and diving, and complete a degree in marine science.' These steps match the profession's work with sea life.

options: He wants to meet famous people

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: A Bad Dream
lessons.notes_html:
Summary

The story A Bad Dream tells of two families — Mr Aziz's family, who planned the holiday, and Mr Karim's family, who decided to join them. They planned a 10-day trip and travelled by train to the station called Patni. From there they hired a van to reach the house they had rented for ten days. The porter at the station and then the van driver were surprised on hearing the address, and the driver told Mr Aziz that the house was haunted, but Mr Aziz said he did not believe such stories. Everybody liked the house: it was big and airy, with three bedrooms and a nice view of the village and the fields, and the children got the biggest room. They enjoyed the clean air of the village and fresh vegetables from the fields, felt happy and relaxed, and did not want to go back. Some villagers asked them to leave the house before the ghosts harmed them, but they laughed and said there was no such thing as ghosts. Nothing happened for a few days; then, on the seventh night, strange things started happening. All three strange happenings were Mr Karim's: someone pulling his blanket and bed; a head jumping and blocking his way on a walk; and finally an empty chair moving by itself, seen by all four adults. On the last morning they got out of bed very early and quickly left for the station — but in the end Mr Karim woke up screaming and found that the whole trip had been a dream. None of the children experienced anything strange.

Key Points

  • Two families went on the trip: Mr Aziz's and Mr Karim's.
  • On hearing where they were staying, two people — first the porter, then the driver — asked whether they were sure.
  • After an early dinner they went to bed quite early, as they were tired; the next morning, after breakfast, they went into the fields.
  • First Mr Karim, then Mr Karim again, and finally all four adults had the strange experiences.
  • What happened in the end of the story: it was all a dream — a bad dream.

Vocabulary

hauntedhaving presence of ghosts (Para 5)
scaredfrightened (Para 10)
gossipconversation that may not be true (Para 11)
dominatehave power or influence over something (Para 11)
imaginingform a mental picture (Para 11)

An Alternative Ending

The family stayed on in the house and found natural explanations for everything: a stray cat had pulled the blanket, the 'head' was the shadow of a hanging lantern, and the chair had been moved by a loose floorboard. They laughed at their fears and enjoyed the rest of their holiday happily.

Remember

In Exercise 7, groups develop a role-play on a good dream, for example a dream of flying: 'Dreams teach us to aim high… Fly high, but remember to come back home!' — we must work hard to make our dreams come true.

lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 5.2 Oral Communication teaches presentation evaluation: first prepare a presentation following the presentation guidelines of Unit 4.2, then evaluate the presentations of your colleagues using a rubric with five grades — excellent, good, fair, satisfactory, poor.

Model Presentation: The Impact of Fake News on People's Lives

Good morning, everyone. My name is Ahmed, your class fellow. Today, I would like to talk about the impact of fake news on people's lives. I will probably take about five minutes. I have divided my topic into three parts. First, what is fake news: false news shared to mislead people. Secondly, its impact: it spreads fear, creates quarrels, harms innocent people, and makes people believe wrong things. For example, a false message about a school closure can waste everyone's time. Lastly, what we can do: check news before sharing, trust only reliable sources, and never forward unverified messages. In conclusion, we must stop fake news by thinking before we share. Thank you for your time.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Revision of Number of Nouns
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

Most nouns form the plural by adding -s (train – trains, bank – banks). Nouns ending in a hissing sound add -es (dish – dishes, witch – witches). Nouns ending in consonant + y change y to -ies (story – stories, theory – theories, city – cities), but vowel + y only adds -s (essay – essays, valley – valleys, chimney – chimneys, donkey – donkeys, boy – boys). Many nouns ending in -f/-fe change to -ves (leaf – leaves, thief – thieves, knife – knives, calf – calves, hoof – hooves). Some nouns ending in -o add -es (potato – potatoes, tomato – tomatoes), others only -s (portfolio – portfolios, studio – studios). Irregular plurals change the vowel or the word: child – children, tooth – teeth, woman – women, ox – oxen, foot – feet, mouse – mice. Compound nouns pluralise the main word: son-in-law – sons-in-law, father-in-law – fathers-in-law, secretary of state – secretaries of state, check-up – check-ups. Some nouns are the same in singular and plural (sheep, deer, police, hair), some are uncountable (news), and some are used only in the plural (trousers).

Plurals Practised

Examples

My father-in-law is kind. Our fathers-in-law are friends.compound noun: main word plural

Remember

'Hair' is usually uncountable (She has long hair), but 'a hair' is used for a single strand (I found a hair on my shirt). 'News' looks plural but is uncountable and stays 'news'.

mcqs.q: How do most nouns form the plural?
mcqs.why: Most nouns form the plural by adding -s: train – trains, bank – banks. Special rules apply only to nouns with particular endings, such as hissing sounds, consonant + y, and -f/-fe.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'story'?
mcqs.why: Nouns ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: story – stories, theory – theories, city – cities. But vowel + y only adds -s, as in essay – essays and boy – boys.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'essay'?
mcqs.why: Because 'essay' ends in vowel + y (a + y), it only adds -s: essays. Valleys, chimneys, donkeys and boys follow the same rule, unlike story and city.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'leaf'?
mcqs.why: Many nouns ending in -f/-fe change to -ves: leaf – leaves, thief – thieves, knife – knives, calf – calves, hoof – hooves. So 'leafs' is wrong even though it looks regular.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'potato'?
mcqs.why: Some nouns ending in -o add -es: potato – potatoes, tomato – tomatoes, as in 'Please buy some potatoes and tomatoes.' Others, like portfolio and studio, only add -s.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'child'?
mcqs.why: 'Child – children' is an irregular plural: the word itself changes instead of adding -s or -es. Other irregular plurals in the lesson are tooth – teeth, foot – feet, mouse – mice and ox – oxen.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'son-in-law'?
mcqs.why: Compound nouns pluralise the main word: son-in-law – sons-in-law, father-in-law – fathers-in-law, secretary of state – secretaries of state. The main word here is 'son', so it alone becomes plural.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'sheep'?
mcqs.why: Some nouns are the same in singular and plural: sheep, deer, police, hair. The example says Farmer Abdul Raheem has three sheep and four deer on his farm, with no change in form.

options: It is a regular plural noun
It looks plural but is uncountable and stays 'news'
It is used only for one item
mcqs.q: What is special about the noun 'news'?
mcqs.why: The Remember section warns: 'news' looks plural but is uncountable and stays 'news'. It is listed among the nouns that keep the same form, like hair and trousers (used only in the plural).

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'cliff'?
mcqs.why: Not every -f noun changes to -ves: the practised plurals give cliff – cliffs, with simple -s, as in 'I saw three big oxen near the cliffs.' The -ves change applies to many, not all, -f/-fe nouns.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Modal Verbs
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

Modal verbs change plain statements into polite requests, advice and permission. For requests, use Could you… please? / Would you…? / May I…?: 'Shut the door' becomes 'Could you shut the door, please, as it is windy today?'; 'Send me an email' becomes 'Would you send me an email so that I can follow it up?' For advice, use should (You should listen to your mother), should not for negative advice (You should not break traffic rules), ought to for a duty (You ought to fulfil the promise you made to your mother), and had better for advice with a warning (You had better finish your task on time or you'll be in trouble). For permission, use May I…?: 'May I have half-day leave, Sir, as there is an emergency in my family?'

Statements into Requests

StatementRequest
Shut the door, as it is windy today.Could you shut the door, please, as it is windy today?
Help me finish this assignment.Could you help me finish this assignment, please?
Pass the salt and pepper.Could you pass the salt and pepper, please?
Repeat what you just said.Could you repeat what you just said, please?
Clear the table so that I can put my computer there.Could you clear the table so that I can put my computer there?
Show me how to fix this problem.Could you show me how to fix this problem?
Move this chair in the corner.Could you move this chair into the corner, please?

Statements into Advice

StatementAdvice
Listen to your mother.You should listen to your mother.
Give good reason for your absence.You should give a good reason for your absence.
Break traffic rules.You should not break traffic rules.
Fulfil the promise you made to your mother.You ought to fulfil the promise you made to your mother.
Finish your task on time or you'll be in trouble.You had better finish your task on time or you'll be in trouble.
Talk when others are speaking.You should not talk when others are speaking.
Follow the instructions carefully.You should follow the instructions carefully.

Requests and Advice for Situations

  • You need a pen, and your sister has one — Request: Could you lend me your pen, please?
  • You spend too much money on unnecessary clothes — Advice: You should not spend so much money on unnecessary clothes.
  • Your friend leads an unhealthy lifestyle — Advice: You ought to live a healthy lifestyle. You should eat healthy food and exercise daily.
  • You want to go with your brother to the stadium — Request: May I go with you to the stadium to watch the cricket match?
  • Your friend told you a family secret — Advice: You should not tell anyone your friend's secret.
  • The phone rings while you are cooking and your father is near it — Request: Could you answer the phone, please?
  • It is hot and you are thirsty — Request: Could you give me a glass of water, please?
  • Your brother plays loud music while you study — Request: Could you please turn the music down? I am studying for an exam.

Remember

Pattern: request = Could you / Would you / May I + base verb; advice = should / ought to / had better + base verb; negative advice = should not + base verb.

options: 'Could you shut the door, please, as it is windy today?'
mcqs.q: How can the command 'Shut the door' be made into a polite request?
mcqs.why: For requests we use Could you… please? / Would you…? / May I…? The table converts it to: 'Could you shut the door, please, as it is windy today?' Modal verbs turn plain statements into polite requests.

mcqs.q: Which modal is used for ordinary advice, as in 'You ___ listen to your mother'?
mcqs.why: For advice we use 'should': 'You should listen to your mother.' Negative advice uses 'should not', as in 'You should not break traffic rules' and 'You should not talk when others are speaking.'

mcqs.q: 'You ___ fulfil the promise you made to your mother' — which modal shows a duty?
mcqs.why: The lesson uses 'ought to' for a duty: 'You ought to fulfil the promise you made to your mother.' It is also the advice given for leading a healthy lifestyle: 'You ought to live a healthy lifestyle.'

mcqs.q: Which modal gives advice with a warning?
mcqs.why: 'Had better' gives advice with a warning: 'You had better finish your task on time or you'll be in trouble.' The 'or you'll be in trouble' part is the warning that makes this form stronger than 'should'.

options: 'May I have half-day leave, Sir, as there is an emergency in my family?'
mcqs.q: How do you ask permission using a modal?
mcqs.why: For permission we use May I…?: 'May I have half-day leave, Sir, as there is an emergency in my family?' The same form appears in 'May I go with you to the stadium to watch the cricket match?'

options: 'Could you lend me your pen, please?'
mcqs.q: Your sister has a pen and you need one. What is the polite request in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The situations section gives exactly this request: 'Could you lend me your pen, please?' The pattern for requests is Could you / Would you / May I + base verb, as the Remember section sums up.

options: You should not spend so much money on unnecessary clothes
mcqs.q: What advice is given to someone who spends too much on unnecessary clothes?
mcqs.why: The advice is negative advice with 'should not': 'You should not spend so much money on unnecessary clothes.' 'Should not + base verb' is the pattern for negative advice in this lesson.

mcqs.q: The phone rings while you are cooking and your father is near it. What request does the lesson give?
mcqs.why: The situation's request is: 'Could you answer the phone, please?' It follows the same Could you pattern used for passing the salt and pepper and clearing the table.

options: 'Could you please turn the music down? I am studying for an exam.'
mcqs.q: Your brother plays loud music while you study. What should you say?
mcqs.why: The lesson's request for this situation is: 'Could you please turn the music down? I am studying for an exam.' Giving the reason after the request makes it polite and clear.

mcqs.q: What is the pattern for negative advice?
mcqs.why: The Remember section gives the patterns: request = Could you / Would you / May I + base verb; advice = should / ought to / had better + base verb; negative advice = should not + base verb.

lessons.title: Writing: Letter to the Editor (Revision)
lessons.notes_html:
Format of a Letter to the Editor

  1. Begin by writing the date on the left side.
  2. Under the date write 'The Editor'.
  3. Then write the name of the newspaper.
  4. Add the name of the city.
  5. Begin by addressing the person, i.e., Dear Sir/Madam.
  6. Come directly to the main point.
  7. Explain why the topic is important, with evidence.
  8. State your opinion about what should be done.
  9. Sign the letter. (General rule for the whole letter: keep it brief.)

Model Letter: Stagnant Water on Roads and Streets

17 October 2026. The Editor, Daily Dawn, Karachi. Dear Sir, I write to draw your attention to the problem of stagnant water on the roads and streets of our area. After every rain, water stands on the roads for days. It blocks the way, spreads bad smell, and breeds mosquitoes, which cause malaria and dengue. Children and old people suffer the most. The concerned authorities should clean the drains and repair the roads at once. I hope this letter will wake them up to their duty. Yours truly, Ahmed Raza.

Model Letter: Unannounced Load-Shedding

17 October 2026. The Editor, Daily Dawn, Karachi. Dear Sir, I write to highlight the problem of unannounced load-shedding in our area. Electricity goes off again and again without any notice, even at night. Students cannot study, patients suffer, and business comes to a standstill. Water supply also stops because motors cannot run. The authorities should announce a fixed load-shedding schedule and follow it strictly. I hope this letter will draw the attention of the concerned officials to this serious problem. Yours truly, Ahmed Raza.

Remember

A letter to the editor is short and public-minded: date, The Editor, newspaper, city, Dear Sir/Madam, the problem at once, why it matters, what should be done, and the sign-off 'Yours truly' with your name.

mcqs.why: After the date, 'The Editor', the newspaper name and the city, the letter begins by addressing the person: Dear Sir/Madam. Both model letters use 'Dear Sir' in this position.

mcqs.why: The format says: come directly to the main point, then explain why the topic is important with evidence, and state your opinion about what should be done. The general rule for the whole letter is to keep it brief.

mcqs.q: How do the model letters to the editor sign off?
mcqs.why: Both model letters close with 'Yours truly, Ahmed Raza.' The Remember section also lists the sign-off 'Yours truly' with your name as part of the letter's format.

mcqs.why: Both letters are addressed: 'The Editor, Daily Dawn, Karachi', dated 17 October 2026. The format requires the newspaper's name followed by the name of the city.

mcqs.why: It states the opinion clearly: the concerned authorities should clean the drains and repair the roads at once. Stating what should be done is a required step in the letter's format.

mcqs.why: The letter highlights unannounced load-shedding: electricity goes off again and again without any notice, even at night. Students cannot study, patients suffer, business comes to a standstill, and water supply also stops.

mcqs.why: The writer's opinion is that the authorities should announce a fixed load-shedding schedule and follow it strictly. The letter hopes to draw the attention of the concerned officials to this serious problem.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Speak Gently
lessons.notes_html:
Summary

The poem Speak Gently teaches us to speak gently to all people. Its main idea is that speaking gently wins people's love: it is better to rule by love than by fear, and harsh words spoil (mar) the good we may do. Speaking gently is a small thing, but an important one, whose good and joy will be told by eternity. We can earn respect from people by speaking gently, behaving kindly, helping others, and never hurting anyone with our words.

Key Points from the Verses

VerseWhat we should doResult
Verse 1Speak gently; let no harsh words passIt is better to rule by love than by fear; harsh words spoil the good we may do
Verse 2Speak gently to the little child; teach it in soft and mild accentsIt wins the child's love; the child may not remain a child for long
Verse 3Speak gently to the aged one; do not grieve the care-worn heartLet such depart in peace; their sands of life are nearly run — old people will leave the world shortly
Verse 4Speak gently — a little thing dropped in the heart's deep wellThe good and joy it may bring, eternity shall tell; only time will show its impact on people's lives

Vocabulary

WordMeaning
gentlysoftly and kindly
harshrude or rough
marspoil
accentstone of voice
agedold
grievecause unhappiness
careworntired
eternityunending time / forever

Small Things That Give Happiness or Hurt

  • Give happiness: smile at others; say 'thank you'; help a friend; praise others; share things; listen politely; apologise for a mistake.
  • Can hurt: frown at others; speak harshly; laugh at a friend's mistake; insult others; take others' things; interrupt others; blame others for your mistake.
  • Model promise: 'I will help my classmates in their studies to give them happiness, and I will never interrupt others while they are speaking, so that I do not hurt them.'

Remember

Speak gently — to everyone, to little children in a soft manner, and to old people so as not to cause them unhappiness. It is a small but important thing.

options: Speaking gently wins people's love; it is better to rule by love than by fear
mcqs.q: What is the main idea of the poem 'Speak Gently'?
mcqs.why: The summary gives the main idea: speaking gently wins people's love, it is better to rule by love than by fear, and harsh words spoil (mar) the good we may do. The whole poem teaches gentle speech.

options: They make the child silent forever
mcqs.q: What happens when we speak gently to a little child?
mcqs.why: Verse 2 says: speak gently to the little child and teach it in soft and mild accents; it wins the child's love. The verse also reminds us that the child may not remain a child for long.

options: Grieve the care-worn heart with complaints
Do not grieve the care-worn heart; let such depart in peace
mcqs.q: How should we speak to the aged one, according to Verse 3?
mcqs.why: Verse 3 says: speak gently to the aged one and do not grieve the care-worn heart; let such depart in peace, because their sands of life are nearly run — old people will leave the world shortly.

options: It will be forgotten in a day
The good and joy it may bring, eternity shall tell — only time will show its impact
mcqs.q: What does Verse 4 say about a gentle word?
mcqs.why: Verse 4 calls it a little thing dropped in the heart's deep well: the good and joy it may bring, eternity shall tell. The table explains: only time will show its impact on people's lives.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'mar' mean in the poem?
mcqs.why: The vocabulary list gives mar = spoil, as in the line that harsh words spoil the good we may do. Other poem words are gently = softly and kindly, harsh = rude or rough, and eternity = unending time.

mcqs.q: Which small action gives happiness, according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: The happiness list includes: smile at others, say 'thank you', help a friend, praise others, share things, listen politely, and apologise for a mistake. Frowning, laughing at mistakes and interrupting are listed as things that can hurt.

mcqs.q: Which action can hurt others?
mcqs.why: The hurt list includes: frown at others, speak harshly, laugh at a friend's mistake, insult others, take others' things, interrupt others, and blame others for your mistake. Interrupting is one of these hurtful actions.

options: By speaking the loudest in class
By speaking gently, behaving kindly, helping others, and never hurting anyone with our words
mcqs.q: How can we earn respect from people, as the summary says?
mcqs.why: The summary states: we can earn respect from people by speaking gently, behaving kindly, helping others, and never hurting anyone with our words. Respect comes from gentleness, not from fear.

options: 'I will help my classmates in their studies and never interrupt others while they are speaking'
'I will speak loudly so all can hear'
'I will correct everyone's mistakes at once'
'I will talk only to my friends'
mcqs.q: What is the model promise in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The model promise reads: 'I will help my classmates in their studies to give them happiness, and I will never interrupt others while they are speaking, so that I do not hurt them.' It joins one happiness-giving act with one hurt-avoiding act.

mcqs.q: What do 'accents' mean in the poem's vocabulary?
mcqs.why: The vocabulary gives accents = tone of voice, as in teaching the child 'in soft and mild accents'. Other words are aged = old, grieve = cause unhappiness, and careworn = tired.

lessons.title: Oral Communication: Public Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 6.2 Oral Communication teaches public speaking. In Exercise 1 you describe something you own which is very important to you, answering the Wh-questions: Where did you get it from? How long have you had it? Who gave it to you? When did you purchase it? Why did you purchase it? Why is it important to you? In Exercise 2 you prepare a three-minute speech following the public-speaking rules: opening greeting, introduction of the topic, ordered points (First, Second, Third), and a conclusion with thanks.

Model Description: My Watch

Good morning, everyone. Today I will tell you about something I own which is very important to me: my watch. I got it from my grandfather. He gave it to me on my tenth birthday, so I have had it for two years. I did not purchase it; it was a gift. It is important to me because it was my grandfather's own watch, and it reminds me of him and teaches me the value of time.

Model Speech: The Importance of a Clean Environment

Good morning, everyone. Today I will speak about the importance of a clean environment. A clean environment means clean air, clean water, and clean surroundings. First, a clean environment keeps us healthy: dirty surroundings spread diseases like malaria and dengue. Second, it keeps our minds fresh and happy: we feel good in clean places. Third, it protects animals, birds and plants. So, we must not throw litter on roads and in streets. We must plant trees and keep our school and homes clean. In conclusion, a clean environment is a healthy environment. Let us all play our part in keeping it clean. Thank you.

Remember

Answer every Wh-question in a description talk, and in a speech keep the pattern: greet, state the topic, give points in order, conclude, thank the audience.

options: Wh-questions about it, such as where you got it, who gave it to you, and why it is important
mcqs.q: In Exercise 1 of public speaking, what do you answer about something you own?
mcqs.why: You describe something you own which is very important to you, answering the Wh-questions: Where did you get it from? How long have you had it? Who gave it to you? When did you purchase it? Why is it important to you?

mcqs.q: How long is the speech prepared in Exercise 2?
mcqs.why: In Exercise 2 you prepare a three-minute speech following the public-speaking rules: opening greeting, introduction of the topic, ordered points (First, Second, Third), and a conclusion with thanks.

He bought it himself last year

He found it in a shop

mcqs.why: The model says: 'I got it from my grandfather. He gave it to me on my tenth birthday, so I have had it for two years. I did not purchase it; it was a gift.'

options: It tells the correct time only
It was his grandfather's own watch; it reminds him of his grandfather and teaches him the value of time
mcqs.q: Why is the watch important to the speaker?
mcqs.why: He says it is important because it was his grandfather's own watch, and it reminds him of his grandfather and teaches him the value of time. Its value is in the memories, not in gold or newness.

options: A clean environment keeps us healthy: dirty surroundings spread diseases like malaria and dengue
It has no effect on health
mcqs.q: What is the first point of the model speech on a clean environment?
mcqs.why: The speech's first point is: a clean environment keeps us healthy, because dirty surroundings spread diseases like malaria and dengue. The second point is fresh and happy minds, and the third is protection of animals, birds and plants.

mcqs.q: What does the model speech ask us to do?
mcqs.why: The speech urges: we must not throw litter on roads and in streets; we must plant trees and keep our school and homes clean. Its conclusion is that a clean environment is a healthy environment.

options: Greet, state the topic, give points in order, conclude, thank the audience
Tell a joke, then sit down
Read the speech from a book
mcqs.q: What pattern should a speech keep, according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: The Remember section gives the pattern: greet, state the topic, give points in order, conclude, thank the audience. The description talk, in turn, must answer every Wh-question.

options: It keeps our minds fresh and happy: we feel good in clean places
mcqs.q: What is the second point of the clean-environment speech?
mcqs.why: Second, a clean environment keeps our minds fresh and happy: we feel good in clean places. Third, it protects animals, birds and plants — this order of points is how the model speech is organised.

mcqs.q: What does a clean environment protect, in the third point?
mcqs.why: The third point of the model speech is that a clean environment protects animals, birds and plants. The speech closes with 'Let us all play our part in keeping it clean. Thank you.'

options: 'My watch is two years old and golden'

'Today I will tell you about something I own which is very important to me: my watch' opens the model description

lessons.title: Language Practice: Transitional Devices Showing Order and Reason
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

Transitional devices join ideas smoothly. Words showing order (sequence) in the book's passages are: First, Then, Next, After that, As soon as — and also Step one / Step two / Step three, Meanwhile, Before, Later, Finally, In the end, Afterwards. Connectors of reason are: because, as, since, owing to, due to. Use order words when describing a process or a story, and reason connectors when giving causes.

Order Words in Use

SentenceDevice
My sister was in the dentist's office for ten minutes. Meanwhile, I sat in the waiting room with an old magazine in my hands.Meanwhile (at the same time)
An hour passed, but there was no sign of Mujahid. Finally, we decided to go home.Finally
We bumped into Salim during our trip to Keenjhar Lake. A few weeks later, we met him again.later
She had finished her lunch before I had even started.before
They went to a nearby restaurant for breakfast; after that, they drove off towards the River Indus.after that
The football coach announced to play with Sindh first, and then with Baluchistan.first – then
As we are all hungry, we will go to the park before taking lunch.before

A Process in Order: Frying an Egg

First, take a frying pan. Step two, put some oil in it. Step three, put it on the stove. Next, break the egg. After that, put it in the heated oil. Then, cook for a while. After that, sprinkle salt and pepper over it. Finally, put the fried egg on the plate. In the end, eat it with bread.

A Story in Order: The Birthday Passage

Yesterday was my birthday, and it didn't start well. I went to the park to meet my friends, but they weren't there. First, I went to the shopping centre opposite the park, but they weren't there. Then, I looked for them in the library. Next, I tried the sports centre and the restaurant near the park. Finally, I went home, and my friends were there, with a birthday cake, ice cream, music, and games. It was a surprise party for me! In the end, I had a great birthday.

Remember

Pattern for a process: First / Step one → Step two → Step three → Next → After that → Then → Finally → In the end. For reasons use because, as, since, owing to and due to.

options: Words that show sequence, such as First, Then, Next and Finally
mcqs.q: What are transitional devices showing order?
mcqs.why: Transitional devices join ideas smoothly, and words showing order (sequence) include First, Then, Next, After that, As soon as, Meanwhile, Before, Later, Finally and Afterwards. Use order words when describing a process or a story.

mcqs.q: Which device means 'at the same time'?
mcqs.why: The example explains: 'My sister was in the dentist's office for ten minutes. Meanwhile, I sat in the waiting room…' — Meanwhile shows something happening at the same time, not in sequence.

options: because, as, since, owing to and due to
mcqs.q: Which set contains connectors of reason?
mcqs.why: Connectors of reason are because, as, since, owing to and due to; they are used when giving causes. Order words like first, then and finally are used for processes and stories instead.

options: Finally, in 'An hour passed, but there was no sign of Mujahid. ___, we decided to go home'
mcqs.q: Which example uses 'Finally' correctly as given in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The table's example is: 'An hour passed, but there was no sign of Mujahid. Finally, we decided to go home.' Finally marks the last step after waiting, a typical order device.

mcqs.q: In the process of frying an egg, what is the very first step?
mcqs.why: The process begins: 'First, take a frying pan. Step two, put some oil in it. Step three, put it on the stove. Next, break the egg.' The order of the steps matters in a process description.

options: Put it in the heated oil
Sprinkle salt and pepper over it
mcqs.q: After putting the pan on the stove, what comes next in frying an egg?
mcqs.why: The sequence is: First the pan, Step two the oil, Step three the pan on the stove, Next break the egg, After that put it in the heated oil, Then cook for a while, Finally put it on the plate.

options: He found his friends at the shopping centre
His friends were at his home with a birthday cake, ice cream, music and games — a surprise party
His friends had gone to another city
mcqs.q: In the birthday passage, what happened finally?
mcqs.why: After searching the shopping centre, library, sports centre and restaurant, he finally went home, and his friends were there with a birthday cake, ice cream, music and games. It was a surprise party for him.

options: 'Before' in 'She had finished her lunch before I had even started'
mcqs.q: Which shows 'before' used for order?
mcqs.why: The table gives 'She had finished her lunch before I had even started' as the 'before' example. Before can show that one action happened earlier than another in a sequence.

options: First / Step one → Step two → Step three → Next → After that → Then → Finally → In the end
mcqs.q: What is the pattern for describing a process?
mcqs.why: The Remember section gives the process pattern: First / Step one → Step two → Step three → Next → After that → Then → Finally → In the end. The frying-an-egg passage follows exactly this chain.

options: The coach announced the team list
The football coach announced to play with Sindh first, and then with Baluchistan
They drove to the River Indus
mcqs.q: Which sentence uses 'first – then' for order?
mcqs.why: The table's first–then example is the football coach announcing to play with Sindh first, and then with Baluchistan. The 'after that' example is the group driving towards the River Indus after breakfast.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Revision of Direct and Indirect Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

When reporting a question, use asked and change the question into a statement word order (no question mark, no inversion). For yes/no questions, join with if or whether: 'Do you sell seafood?' → She asked him if he sold seafood. For wh-questions, keep the wh-word as the joining word: 'Where is the nearest hospital?' → The old woman asked where the nearest hospital was. Change the tense back (present → past, will → would, can → could, has visited → had visited), change pronouns to match the speaker, and change time/place words (here → there, this → that): 'Can we take photographs here?' → The students asked the caretaker if they could take photographs there.

Yes/No Questions Reported

DirectIndirect
Ali's friend said, 'Can you spare me your book for a week?'Ali's friend asked Ali if he could spare him his book for a week.
She said to him, 'Do you sell seafood?'She asked him if he sold seafood.
'Have you visited Mohatta Palace in Karachi, Charles?' said Behram.Behram asked Charles if he had visited Mohatta Palace in Karachi.
Rehan said to his sister, 'Was your friend's birthday on Friday or Saturday?'Rehan asked his sister whether her friend's birthday was on Friday or Saturday.
The doctor said to his patient, 'Are you taking medicine regularly?'The doctor asked his patient if he was taking medicine regularly.
Ashok said, 'Is there a petrol pump nearby, Sunil?'Ashok asked Sunil if there was a petrol pump nearby.
Mother said, 'Do they know the date of our visit?'Mother asked if they knew the date of our visit.

Wh-Questions Reported

DirectIndirect
'When will your results be announced?' said Jason.Jason asked when his results would be announced.
'What time will the match start, Zaheer?' said Zaman.Zaman asked Zaheer what time the match would start.
The climber said, 'How quickly can we climb this hill?'The climber asked how quickly they could climb that hill.
'What is the price of this article?' the customer asked the shopkeeper.The customer asked the shopkeeper what the price of that article was.
'Why are you angry with me, Zahida?' said Sabiha.Sabiha asked Zahida why she was angry with her.
The policeman said, 'Whose car is this?'The policeman asked whose car that was.
The old man said, 'Children, who broke this windowpane?'The old man asked the children who had broken that windowpane.

Reporting an Interview

Faiz reports his job interview: 'She asked me what my qualification was. She asked me if I knew how to type. She asked me if I could use the computer. She asked me how good my English was. She asked me if I had worked anywhere else before. She asked me why I wanted to work in that factory. She asked me where I lived. She asked me how far that factory was from my house. She asked me if there was any question that I wanted to ask.'

Remember

Reported questions have statement order and a full stop: asked + if/whether (yes/no) or the wh-word (wh-question), with tense, pronoun and here/this changes. Exercise 8 rewrites the whole Nadeem-and-his-boss passage in reported speech the same way.

options: Keep the question mark and question order
Use 'asked' and change the question into statement word order, with no question mark and no inversion
Change everything to the future tense
mcqs.q: When reporting a question, what must you do?
mcqs.why: The rules say: use 'asked' and change the question into a statement word order (no question mark, no inversion). Reported questions end with a full stop, as the Remember section confirms.

options: Use a comma and quotation marks
mcqs.q: How are yes/no questions reported?
mcqs.why: For yes/no questions, join with if or whether: 'Do you sell seafood?' becomes 'She asked him if he sold seafood.' Wh-questions instead keep the wh-word as the joining word.

options: asked where was the nearest hospital?
asked where is the nearest hospital
asked where the nearest hospital was
mcqs.q: 'Where is the nearest hospital?' reported correctly is: The old woman…
mcqs.why: Wh-questions keep the wh-word and change to statement order with the tense moved back: 'The old woman asked where the nearest hospital was.' There is no inversion and no question mark in the reported form.

options: here stays here; this stays this
mcqs.q: What changes happen to time and place words in reported questions?
mcqs.why: The rules list the changes: tense moves back (will → would, can → could, has visited → had visited), pronouns change to match the speaker, and place words change: here → there, this → that.

mcqs.q: 'Can we take photographs here?' — the students asked the caretaker if they…
mcqs.why: The reported form given is: 'The students asked the caretaker if they could take photographs there.' Can becomes could, we becomes they, and here becomes there.

options: Behram asked Charles if he had visited Mohatta Palace in Karachi
Behram asked Charles if he has visited Mohatta Palace
Charles asked Behram if he had visited Mohatta Palace
Behram said Charles had visited Mohatta Palace?
mcqs.q: 'Have you visited Mohatta Palace in Karachi, Charles?' said Behram. Reported:
mcqs.why: The table gives: 'Behram asked Charles if he had visited Mohatta Palace in Karachi.' The present perfect 'have visited' moves back to the past perfect 'had visited' in reported speech.

options: whether (for the choice between Friday or Saturday)
mcqs.q: Rehan asked his sister ___ her friend's birthday was on Friday or Saturday. Which joining word is used?
mcqs.why: The reported sentence in the table uses 'whether': 'Rehan asked his sister whether her friend's birthday was on Friday or Saturday.' Whether suits a choice between two options, Friday or Saturday.

options: Jason asked when will his results be announced?
Jason asked when would his results be announced
Jason asked when his results would be announced
Jason asked when are his results announced
mcqs.q: 'When will your results be announced?' said Jason. Reported correctly:
mcqs.why: The table gives: 'Jason asked when his results would be announced.' Will moves back to would, your becomes his, and the word order becomes statement order with a full stop.

options: She asked what his qualification is
She asked me what my qualification was
She asked me what was my qualification
She said me what my qualification was?
mcqs.q: In Faiz's interview report, how did he report 'What is your qualification?'
mcqs.why: Faiz reports: 'She asked me what my qualification was.' The wh-word is kept, is becomes was, and your becomes my to match the speaker, Faiz himself.

options: Statement order and a full stop
Question order and a question mark
Inverted order and an exclamation mark
mcqs.q: Reported questions end with:
mcqs.why: The Remember section is explicit: reported questions have statement order and a full stop — asked + if/whether for yes/no questions, or the wh-word for wh-questions, with tense, pronoun and here/this changes.

lessons.title: Writing: Expository Essay
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 6.4 Writing teaches the expository essay — an essay that explains a topic with facts and ideas. The sample essay, 'The Hazards of Movie Going', shows the structure: an introductory paragraph ending with a thesis statement that lists the ideas to be covered; body paragraphs, each with a topic sentence, a controlling idea and supporting details; and a concluding paragraph that sums up, beginning with a signalling phrase such as 'In short'. The introduction and the conclusion mention the same ideas: the introduction presents them, the conclusion sums them up and gives the final judgment.

Anatomy of the Sample Essay

PartContent in 'The Hazards of Movie Going'
Thesis (last sentence of the introduction)Three ideas: problems in getting to and inside the theatre; the theatre seating; the behaviour of some movie-goers
Body paragraph 1 topic sentenceOne reason why people prefer watching movies on the TV rather than going to the theatre is the time required in reaching and getting inside the theatre
Body paragraph 2 topic sentenceEven if one manages to get a ticket, there is the problem of getting a good, comfortable seat
Body paragraph 3 topic sentenceFurthermore, there are numerous other problems one has to face because of the way that many movie goers behave
Supporting detailsLong drive of almost an hour or more; long queues; theatre full before one's turn; narrow and hard seats; springs sticking out from torn seat covers; tilting seats; tall person blocking the view; loud comments, whistling and discussions; little kids racing up and down the aisles
ConclusionSignalling phrase 'In short'; restates the three problems and the final judgment that watching movies on TV is a better option

Model Essay: Acquiring a New Skill

Learning a new skill is a useful and rewarding activity. A skill is an ability that a person learns by practice, such as driving, cooking, speaking a language, or using a computer. Acquiring a new skill needs interest, practice, and patience. The first step in acquiring a new skill is to set a clear goal. A learner should decide what skill to learn and why it is needed. For example, a student may learn computer skills to do school work better. Then, the learner should find a good teacher or learning material and make a regular plan for practice. The second step is regular practice. A skill cannot be learnt in one day. A learner must practise daily, even for a short time. Mistakes are a natural part of learning, and a learner should not give up because of them. The third step is to use the skill in real life. A skill becomes strong only when it is used again and again. A person who learns English should speak and write it daily. In short, acquiring a new skill needs a clear goal, regular practice, and real use. Anyone who follows these steps with patience can learn a new skill and make life better.

Model Essay: Importance of Sports

Sports are an important part of life. They include games like cricket, football, hockey, and badminton. Sports are important for health, character, and education. The first importance of sports is good health. Sports keep the body fit and strong. They make the heart and muscles work well. Students who play sports regularly fall sick less often. Sports also refresh the mind after study. The second importance of sports is character building. Sports teach discipline, teamwork, and fair play. A player learns to follow rules, to work with others, and to accept both victory and defeat. These qualities help a person in every part of life. The third importance of sports is that they bring people together. Sports build friendship between players and between nations. Matches and tournaments give people joy and national pride. In short, sports are important for health, character, and unity. Every student should take part in sports along with studies.

lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 6.5 Study Skills teaches SWOC Analysis — studying yourself under four heads: Strengths (what you do well; your advantages), Weaknesses (what you could improve; what hinders you), Opportunities (things and resources easily available or obtainable), and Challenges (things that can harm you; dangers in your environment). Strengths and weaknesses are inside you; opportunities and challenges are around you.

Guiding Questions

HeadQuestions to askModel answers
StrengthsWhat do you do well? What advantages do you have over others?I read and write English well. I am regular, hardworking and punctual.
WeaknessesWhat could you improve? What are the elements that are hindering you?My spoken English and pronunciation. I feel shy speaking in front of the class.
OpportunitiesWhat things or resources are easily available to you? What can you easily obtain?My school library and my English teacher. English books, a dictionary and learning videos.
ChallengesWhat elements can harm you? What dangers do you face in your external environment?Wasting time on mobile games. Friends who disturb me and make fun of my mistakes.

Model SWOC: Learning the English Language

Strengths: I have a good vocabulary and I study regularly. Weaknesses: My speaking is weak and I fear making mistakes. Opportunities: I have a good English teacher, English books, and English learning videos. Challenges: I get little practice at home and I feel shy speaking English in class.

Use SWOC honestly: build on strengths, improve weaknesses, use opportunities, and face challenges with a plan.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: My Travel Diary — Journey to the Gorakh Hills Station
lessons.notes_html:
Summary

My Travel Diary: Journey to the Gorakh Hills Station is Asif's account of a two-day birthday trip. Knowing his love of travel, his parents decided that his birthday celebration would be held at the Gorakh Hills Station, the highest summit and holiday resort in Sindh, situated at an elevation of 5,690 ft from sea level. The journey began from Karachi: after crossing the toll plaza they got on the Motorway, crossed Nooriabad and then Jamshoro, catching glimpses of the River Indus, with Hyderabad across the river, and stopped at a hotel on Kotri Barrage for breakfast. Then they took the Indus Highway, on the right bank of the Indus, to Sehwan, where they visited the shrine of Lal Shahbaz Qalandar, the highly revered Sufi saint, where people from all walks of life pay homage and seek healing. Lunch was served on the bus: spicy fish caught from the Manchar Lake with fresh sugarcane juice, in nicely packed lunch boxes, and the guide gave flyers to everyone. At the foot of the Gorakh Hills the bus could not climb the steep, zigzag 4-kilometre uphill road, so they transferred to a jeep and reached the top before sunset. Since all the rooms were occupied, they stayed in rented tents. After a light dinner they lit a bonfire under a canopy of stars, played Baetbazi and Chinese whisper, and shared funny stories; the crackling of the wood and the bright stars made time come to a standstill. In the morning the sunrise was spellbinding: clouds floated around and could be touched, the fragrances of herbs tranquilized the senses, and there was a surprise birthday cake with candles, followed by halwa puri breakfast. On the way back they took the Dadu-Moro Bridge route to the greener left bank of the river, stopped at Hala to buy souvenirs, glimpsed Matiari in the distance, passed close by Bhit Shah — the town of the second great saint of the text, Hazrat Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai (RA) — crossed Hyderabad and reached Karachi by the Motorway. Asif deeply appreciated his parents' love and meticulous arrangements.

Key Points

  • Their final destination was the Gorakh Hills, reached before sunset; the trip lasted two days.
  • The Gorakh Hills are the highest place in Sindh, a good holiday place for its awesome natural beauty: sunset views, a canopy of stars, a spellbinding sunrise, floating clouds and fresh air.
  • Many people visit the shrine of Lal Shahbaz Qalandar to seek healing; the two great saints mentioned in the text are Lal Shahbaz Qalandar and Hazrat Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai (RA).
  • There was more greenery on the left side of the river on the return route.
  • According to Ibn-e-Batuta, travelling makes one a good storyteller. Saint Augustine's quotation means the same: 'The world is a book, and those who do not travel read only one page.'

Remember

A travel diary records the journey in order — route, stops, sights, food, night and morning, and the way back — with describing words that praise nature: awesome, colossal, spellbinding, awe-inspiring, tranquil.
